neighbours.label: a word used in its theoretical-science sense (time in physics, common ancestor, interactions), as opposed to its everyday sense
fire: Relativity shows that time runs slower for a clock moving near light speed.
Whales and hippos descend from a common ancestor that lived on land.
Physicists still argue about whether time has a direction at the quantum level.
The strong and electromagnetic interactions are unified in some grand theories.
Genetic data suggest that birds and crocodiles share a common ancestor.
In general relativity, time is woven together with space into one fabric.
Particle collisions reveal how quarks feel the weak interactions.
Some cosmologists propose that time itself began with the Big Bang.
quiet: My watch runs slower when the battery is nearly flat, so I am never on time.
Whales and dolphins are the stars of the aquarium's evening show.
My parents still argue about whether it is time to sell the house.
The social interactions at the party were awkward and brief.
My cousin and I share a common interest in old jazz records.
In the summer, time seems to slow down at my grandmother's farm.
Teachers reward kind interactions between pupils on the playground.
Some families propose that dinner time should begin earlier.
